newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity finishes up, hits contract highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity finishes up, hits contract highs.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures again finished sharply higher Wednesday after all traded months hit new contract highs and front months set new spot contract highs, industry sources said.
Although traders said the electricity contracts were drawing strength from strong natural gas and cold weather in parts of the U.S., some said the price rise may be in part due to some shortcovering.
"At this point it almost seems too emotional to be driven by fundamentals," said one futures broker.

December California Oregon Border (COB) closed up $1.68 at $25.26 after hitting a spot contract high of $25.40, while January ended 97 cents higher at $23.50 after hitting a contract high of $23.65 per megawatt hour (MWh).
Remaining COB deferreds settled between 30 cents and $1.40 higher.
December Palo Verde finished up $2.60 at a new contract high of $25.00, while January finished up $2.25 at a new contract high of $22.50 per MWh.
Remaining PV deferreds settled between 25 cents and $1.50 higher.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 302 COB and 92 PV contracts traded Wednesday.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
